title: Retail / e-commerce analytics
_contract: This file RENAMES and CONTEXTUALISES. It must never assert a cause the engine cannot distinguish. See cli/domains/ai.json for the full reasoning; the short form is that `basis_conflicts` cannot tell an injected factor from an exposed duplicate, so no entry here states which one happened.
_denominator_note: Candidates only, declared with --scale-by. Retail has no single denominator: funnel-stage metrics normalise on sessions, spend metrics on orders, ad metrics on impressions. Declaring several costs about 2% of a run each, so declare every one that plausibly applies rather than guessing.
_exempt_note: Suggested --scale-exempt. Rates and per-order averages are already normalised; dividing them by sessions injects a 1/traffic factor and can make two unrelated rates look near-identical.

basis-conflict.label: Counts moving together on traffic
basis-conflict.consistent_with: a traffic event — a campaign, a promotion, a seasonal peak — lifting every raw count at once, so page views, cart adds and orders rise together without any change in behaviour.
basis-conflict.but_also: a real funnel relationship, or a definitional one: orders divided by sessions IS conversion rate, so if both are on the board that pair will inflate for a correct reason.
basis-conflict.distinguish_by: declare --scale-by sessions and read the per-session view. Counts that only moved with traffic will flatten; behaviour that genuinely changed will not.

trend-confound.label: Everything rises in the same weeks
trend-confound.consistent_with: shared seasonality or a sustained campaign period lifting the whole board.
trend-confound.distinguish_by: the differenced basis, which the headline already uses. The raw-vs-differenced gap is how much of the apparent structure was just the calendar.

subset-sum.label: A total that is its channels added up
subset-sum.consistent_with: a roll-up column — total revenue as the sum of its channels, sitewide sessions as the sum of regions — carrying nothing the parts lack.
subset-sum.but_also: nothing. This is arithmetic, holding on at least 99% of rows.
subset-sum.distinguish_by: not needed. Archive the roll-up, keep the channels. Note the engine protects the parts from archiving: every member of an additive family looks individually redundant, and an unguarded ranking would offer them all.

identity.label: One number on two tiles
identity.consistent_with: a metric and its own restatement — a rate and its complement, a count and its percentage.
identity.but_also: two measures that happen to track each other over this window.
identity.distinguish_by: check a longer window, or a period containing a known disruption. Definitional pairs never separate.

derived-aggregate.label: A best-of or worst-of tile
derived-aggregate.consistent_with: an index taking the max or min across categories. Fully determined by its inputs, yet linearly unpredictable, so naive scoring ranks it as a primary signal.
derived-aggregate.but_also: nothing structural — but which input is currently the extreme may itself be the thing an operator watches.
derived-aggregate.distinguish_by: ask whether anyone acts on the index itself or on knowing which category is driving it.
